article_title: Learning analytics and the Universal Design for Learning (UDL): A clustering approach
citation: Marvin Roski, Ratan Sebastian, Ralph Ewerth, Anett Hoppe, Andreas Nehring. (2024). Learning analytics and the Universal Design for Learning (UDL): A clustering approach. Computers & Education 214 (2024) 105028. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compedu.2024.105028
title: I3Learn web-based learning platform for inclusive ion-bonding chemistry
description: I3Learn is a WordPress-based web learning platform on ion bonding for 9th and 10th-grade inclusive chemistry teaching in Lower Saxony, Germany, designed for 180 minutes of remote, independent learning. Its development was guided by the UDL framework: learners can choose between texts and videos, work on tasks with or without help, and use self-assessments (star ratings), plus a customizable interface, read-aloud function, glossary, simple language, and device-independent access.
requirements: Internet-connected device; the platform is designed for independent learning from home
constraints: Only three UDL-guided elements (multiple representations, tasks with/without help, self-assessment) are measurable in the log files; other elements such as simple language cannot be differentiated in the logs
target_learners: 9th and 10th graders in integrated comprehensive schools and high schools in inclusive chemistry education
target_learning_goals: Understanding ion bonding, including minimum goals (brittleness, ion bonding, ratio formula) and extended goals (nomenclature, salts in everyday life)
examples: 384 learners used at least one of the analyzed UDL-guided elements; almost 500,000 log files were generated during the first half of 2022.
key_sources: Marvin Roski, Ratan Sebastian, Ralph Ewerth, Anett Hoppe, Andreas Nehring. (2024). Learning analytics and the Universal Design for Learning (UDL): A clustering approach. Computers & Education 214 (2024) 105028. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compedu.2024.105028

article_title: Human-Centered Design in Graduate Nursing Education: Outcomes From a Cohort Study.
citation: Holt JM, Talsma A, Lloren JIC, Eljarrah I, Woehrle L, Avdeev I. (2025). Human-Centered Design in Graduate Nursing Education: Outcomes From a Cohort Study. Nurse Educator. https://doi.org/10.1097/NNE.0000000000001778
title: Inquiry, Improvement, and Innovation (I3) Model for Advancing Quality Patient-Centered Care
description: A model developed by Hagle and colleagues that the article uses as a guiding framework to "empower clinicians—across settings—to decide which method will best incorporate evidence or generate new solutions in their practice." The article explains that the I3 Model "includes professional activities for EBP and quality improvement (QI), research studies, and innovation to enhance nursing care" and "establishes the need to prepare graduate nurses to apply the 3 methodologies." In this study it justifies adding innovation alongside the QI and research methods usually taught in graduate nursing curricula, framing the I&HCD workshop as filling the commonly missing innovation component.
requirements: Curricula must incorporate all three methodologies—EBP/QI, research, and innovation—rather than only the QI and research methods instructors frequently teach
constraints: The article states no existing model before the I3 Model reflected all the methods nurses used to improve patient care, quality, safety, and outcomes
target_learning_goals: choosing and applying appropriate improvement and innovation methodologies in clinical practice
examples: The authors used the I3 Model to inform the design of the I&HCD workshop studied with 64 graduate nursing students
key_sources: Holt JM, Talsma A, Lloren JIC, Eljarrah I, Woehrle L, Avdeev I. (2025). Human-Centered Design in Graduate Nursing Education: Outcomes From a Cohort Study. Nurse Educator. https://doi.org/10.1097/NNE.0000000000001778
